statusText: Green. The weekend CME halt continues with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail rests at the low-band floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Tail remains far below the block threshold across the whole projected window. One narrow observation window is flagged across the 22:00-23:30 UTC Sunday futures reopen, where Friday's 11.4bp front-end repricing meets thin initial liquidity and two-way gap risk. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100: a halted market holds tail risk at the low-band floor while Friday's front-end repricing waits to be tested
body:
This assessment falls inside the weekend CME halt, so no live NQ price path exists and no mean-reversion failure can be developing. The anchor is Friday's completed session, re-verified against the Nasdaq-100 quote page this hour: the index opened 29,545.90, reached 29,752.78, fell to 29,383.92 and closed 29,433.43, down 0.70% from a 29,641.60 previous close. That leaves the close roughly 50 points off the low of a 369-point range, a downside reversal inside a finished session. The Nasdaq Composite still ended the week 0.9% higher at 26,402.42 and the S&P 500 closed 7,711.76 for a 0.5% weekly gain, so Friday reads as rotation rather than an extending trend. VIX closed 14.43 inside a 14.13-14.84 range and carried no volatility premium into the weekend.

The refinement this hour is the size of Friday's move at the front end of the curve. The 2-year note yield closed 4.35%, up 11.4 basis points on the session and the highest since July, while the 10-year closed 4.72%, up 4.3 basis points. The Federal Reserve's H.15 release, whose latest observation is 27 August, still shows 4.20% and 4.67% and therefore predates the repricing. A move concentrated in the two-year against a much smaller move in the ten-year is a bear-flattening: it prices policy, not growth. The trigger was Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks that inflation has not meaningfully slowed, after which CME FedWatch odds of a 25bp September hike rose to roughly 55.7-57% from 35.4% the prior day.

That number is not uniform across venues. The Kalshi prediction market prices the same decision near 47%, a gap of about ten points against fed funds futures. Under the calibration used here, dispersion of that kind is uncertainty evidence: it supports Stress and caps Confidence, but it is not price-path evidence and does not move Tail. The counterweight sits in energy, where WTI near $83.44 has shed roughly 4% on the week as the Iran standoff is read as a sanctions confrontation rather than an imminent supply threat, with Persian Gulf exports recovered to 15-16 million barrels daily. A decaying geopolitical risk premium removes an amplifier rather than adding one.

The week ahead is labour-heavy and front-loaded. JOLTS job openings and ISM Manufacturing PMI both print Tuesday at 14:00 UTC, with consensus near 7.273m against a 7.359m prior and 55.3 against 55.6 respectively; ADP follows Wednesday, Broadcom reports after Wednesday's close, and the August employment report lands Friday with payrolls seen near +60,000 after a 23,000 July decline, unemployment at 4.2% and average hourly earnings at +0.2%. None of these is inside the projected 24-hour window, so all are calendar checkpoints rather than current evidence.

Tail therefore stays at the low-band floor of 5 and the mapped policy state is EA_ON. Stress rises one point to 28 on the confirmed front-end repricing against split venue pricing. Confidence rises to 83: current levels, yields, oil, VIX and the verified seven-day calendar are all in hand this hour, with the single acknowledged gap being the absence of any live price path while the market is closed. One narrow observation window is flagged across the projected 22:00-23:30 UTC futures reopen. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was read and found stale at roughly 244 minutes old, so it was not used and the assessment rests entirely on independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, covering the weekend halt from Saturday evening through the hour before this one. The series was uniformly green with Tail fixed at 5, dominant mode normal, and Stress confined to a 25-27 band. Confidence decayed from 68 to 58 through the overnight hours as published evidence aged across the closed market, then recovered steadily through 64, 72 and 80 to 82 as primary sources were re-verified on each hourly refresh. No hour in the window contained an observable NQ price path.
outlookSummary: The next five projected hours remain inside the weekend CME halt, where no price path can form; Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 while Stress drifts from 28 to 29 into the reopen and Confidence decays from 83 to 79 with ageing evidence. From the projected 22:00 UTC reopen the conditional Tail lifts to 12, still inside the low band and far below the block threshold, covering the first live test of a front-end repricing that futures and prediction markets currently price about ten points apart. It then eases through 11 and 10 across the Asian session to an overnight low of 8, recovers through 9 and 10 across the European morning, and reaches a projected peak of 15 across the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open, where opening-auction imbalance meets month-end rebalancing on the final session of August. The window closes at 13 by U.S. midday. Every projected hour maps to EA_ON and green; Stress peaks at 34 in the moderate band and Confidence declines gradually to 65.
